planting.note: Only acquire lab-propagated seedlings from a specialist orchid grower, since wild-collected plants almost never survive transplant; site under conifers in humus-rich, well-drained, duff-covered soil that mimics the dry-shade mountain forests where it grows.

directions: This small Pacific Northwest native produces a short stem bearing a pair of broad, pleated leaves and a cluster of two or more muted maroon-and-yellow-green slipper flowers, an unusual trait among lady's slippers that usually carry a single bloom per stem. It depends on a narrow set of mycorrhizal fungi found in mature coniferous duff, which is why it is counted among the most demanding Cypripedium species to establish away from its native range. Gardeners who succeed with it typically start from laboratory-grown seedlings rather than any wild-dug material, and even then should expect a slow-building, unpredictable clump rather than quick results. It remains a connoisseur's plant, offered only sporadically by a handful of hardy-orchid specialists.
sources: Montana Natural Heritage Program Field Guide

planting.note: Plant nursery-propagated crowns in fall into gritty, humus-rich, neutral-to-alkaline woodland soil that drains quickly yet never dries out, echoing the high-elevation light woodland of its native range.

directions: A high-elevation Yunnan and southeastern Tibet native closely allied to the more familiar Cypripedium tibeticum, this species carries a single rounded, deep rose-pink to white pouch flower above a short stem each late spring. It is noticeably choosier in cultivation than its tibeticum cousin, resenting both waterlogging and summer heat, so growers generally keep it in a sheltered, cool, part-shaded spot with sharp drainage at the root. Division of established clumps in dormancy is the most reliable increase method, since seed-raised stock is slow and still uncommon outside a few hardy-orchid specialist growers. Give it a winter mulch in colder zones and patience, as flowering clumps take years to build.
sources: Royal Botanic Gardens Kew - Plants of the World Online
